sections.html:
The median home value in Tacoma is $479,600, and 55.8 percent of households own rather than rent. About 229,816 people live in the city, which is the county seat of Pierce County and the economic center of the South Sound. If you own a house that tenants occupy, note that median gross rent is $1,676.

Joint Base Lewis-McChord lies several miles south of the city, and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport is 22 miles north in SeaTac. Workers spend an average of 28.8 minutes getting to their jobs, a fact worth putting in a listing description.

Most buyers want to know which part of town a house is in before they ask anything else. The city is grouped into Central Tacoma, New Tacoma around downtown, North Tacoma, Northeast Tacoma, West Tacoma and the Port of Tacoma area, and each has its own character.

  • Central Tacoma includes Hilltop, Delong Park, the Wedge, Bryant and College Heights.
  • North Tacoma includes the Proctor District, the North Slope, Old Tacoma, Ruston Way, Skyline and Yakima Hill.
  • West Tacoma includes the Highlands, Narrows, Titlow and Salmon Beach.
  • Downtown takes in the Stadium District, the Theater District, the Dome District and the Thea Foss Waterway.

Transit shapes demand near the core. The T Line connects Tacoma Dome Station, downtown, the University of Washington Tacoma campus and Hilltop, and Sounder trains and express buses run toward Seattle.

Two boundary points can trip up a seller. Ruston is its own incorporated town and Browns Point is unincorporated, so confirm which jurisdiction your parcel is in before you ask the City of Tacoma about permits. Tacoma also has a historic preservation program, with 165 city landmarks and more than 1,000 historic properties across five overlay zones. If your house is older, ask the city whether it sits in one before you plan exterior work.

Elevation and water do most of the work here. Tacoma ranges from sea level to roughly 500 feet and wraps around Commencement Bay, and many parts of the city have views of Mount Rainier. The low ground near the Port of Tacoma sits in the path of a lahar from the Puyallup River if the volcano ever erupts, so buyers near the tide flats sometimes ask about it.

The odor locals called the Tacoma Aroma ended when the Simpson Tacoma Kraft mill closed in September 2023. Downtown has changed a great deal since the 1990s, with the UW Tacoma campus, the T Line and a restored Thea Foss Waterway, and the Tacoma Narrows bridges link the city to Gig Harbor and the Kitsap Peninsula.

A new property maintenance standard takes effect on January 1, 2027. The City Council passed Ordinance 29125, which brings International Property Maintenance Code standards into the city's Property Maintenance and Nuisance Code and gives the city stronger tools against repeat and chronic violations.

The city handles roughly 4,500 property maintenance cases a year under Chapters 8.30 and 2.01 of its code. Section 7 of the ordinance says the expanded enforcement program starts no earlier than nine months after the council funds it, so the day-to-day effect depends on future budgets.

If you own a vacant, neglected or rental house in Tacoma, ask the city whether any open code complaint is attached to the property before you list. Details are at tacoma.gov/IPMC.

Pierce County bills and collects property tax for Tacoma addresses through the Assessor-Treasurer's office at 2401 S. 35th St., Room 142, in Tacoma. The main number is (253) 798-6111. Because a sale in progress has to settle any unpaid balance and prorate the part of the year the buyer will own, ask the office for a payoff figure early.

Payments can be made in several ways:

  • Online through the parcel search site.
  • By phone at (253) 798-3333.
  • By mail to Pierce County Finance.
  • At the cashier lobby, 1501 Market St., Suite 120, from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays.

Starting in January 2027, more Pierce County homeowners who are 61 or older, or who have a qualifying disability, will see their taxes reduced under an expanded state program. If that describes you or a relative who owns the house, ask the Assessor-Treasurer about it before you sell.

sections.h2: Excise tax and the seller disclosure
sections.html:
Real estate excise tax is due from the seller at the county treasurer on the date of sale. The state portion is 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 of the price and 1.28 percent on the amount between $525,000 and $1,525,000, and a local portion is added.

Under RCW 64.06.020, a seller of most improved residential property must hand the buyer a signed disclosure statement within five business days after both sides sign the contract. The form asks about the roof, plumbing, electrical and heating systems, and it reminds the seller to provide carbon monoxide alarms and at least one smoke detection device.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
• Gather your latest tax statement and any special assessments.
  • Ask the county for the payoff amount on any unpaid taxes.
  • Collect permit records for additions, such as a converted garage or a new bathroom.
  • Check whether the city or the county has an open complaint or lien tied to the parcel.

Having these in a folder before the first showing shortens the back and forth with buyers and the title company. Whatever surfaces during title work, such as a lien or an unpaid balance, gets paid out of your proceeds at closing, so it helps to know the numbers ahead of time.

sections.h2: Should I list my Tacoma house or take a cash offer?
sections.html:
The answer turns on your repair budget, your calendar and how much work the house needs before a buyer's inspector walks through. A listing exposes the house to the open market. A cash offer trades some of that exposure for speed and fewer conditions, which suits a vacant house, an inherited property or a rental with a tenant in place.

Either way, compare written offers on what you net, not on the headline price. Ask each buyer who pays the excise tax, how long the offer stays open, what the closing date is and whether they take the house as it stands with its contents. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and loan approval, so the closing date depends mostly on title work and your own move.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Tacoma that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer may purchase the house as it stands. On most residential sales you still complete the seller disclosure statement describing the property's condition to the best of your knowledge.

faqs.q: What does Ordinance 29125 mean for Tacoma sellers?
faqs.a: It sets a new property maintenance standard that takes effect January 1, 2027. The expanded enforcement program starts no earlier than nine months after the council funds it, so check for open code complaints on your property before you sell.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on a Tacoma house?
faqs.a: Pierce County does, through its Assessor-Treasurer's office in Tacoma. Call (253) 798-6111 for assessed values, statements and exemptions, and ask for a payoff figure before closing.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax when a Tacoma house sells?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays it, and it is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. The state rate is graduated, starting at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000, with a local portion added.

faqs.q: How many people live in Tacoma?
faqs.a: About 229,816 as of July 1, 2025, up from 219,346 at the April 2020 count. Tacoma is the third most populous city in Washington.
